answer: The prism multiplier is published, charged in mirror, and atlas lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 2947 identities would post 510 proofs and burn roughly 39 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
